chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Held up in a Harlem elevator
summary: She tells of two men holding up her building's elevator on 141st Street while she was recording for Okeh, and the caretaker's police whistle.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: HEMLOCK FRAGILE
Where did you live when you were in New York?
I stayed at 141 141st Street and I stayed on Edgecomb (PHONETIC) Street and I stayed three places in New York. I got held up in New York.
Held up?

Uh-huh. I was staying at (unintelligible) take my medicine. I was staying at 141st -- Avenue and 141st Street on the seventh floor and so when I the elevator, the elevator was so long coming in, two men come in , salt and pepper coats, you know, and they holding us up, you know. But the caretaker had given us all police whistles, if something like that happened in there, to blow the whistle and the police would come and protect us, you know.
When was that?
During the time I was staying there, you know.
When was that, the '20s or the '30s?
It must have been the '20s, must have been. It might have been the '30s too. I don't know. But it was during the time I was doing recording O.K.
Oh, then that was the '20s. That's when you did those recordings.
(Inaudible).
And did you blow the whistle?

Yeah, but (unintelligible) I was waiting for the elevator and it was somebody else come in the door. I said, "Thank God," and he (unintelligible) somebody I know and they (unintelligible) they flew out of there. I said, "Thank God," just like that. Child, they was running like mad. I knew what it was.
Do you remember who it was who came?
I don't know (unintelligible).
Oh.
No.
(Laughter.)
Oh, how smart.

How smart I was. (Unintelligible) in the building. I said, "Thank God," and these people flew. And I said -- and when they got there, I say, "Take me as far as the seventh floor," and they took me as far as the seventh floor and let me off and they got off with me, I went into my room. Herschel was staying with me -- I got two rooms (unintelligibile) for Herschel and I stayed over here with a girl. Her name was Susie. (Unintelligible) and I rented a room for Herschel.
That was a hotel. Was that a hotel?
Apartment house, you know.
Apartment house, huh?
Either a hotel or apartment house. And
we got a big building down on Avenue and 141st Street, right on the corner, Avenue and 141st Street. Jimmy Amos (PHONETIC) stayed -- used to come up there all the time.
Who?

Jimmy (unintelligible), Jimmy Amos. I know you don't remember, but (inaudible). He used to come up there all the time. And so they told me, say, "Don't never go out alone when you go out at night." (Unintelligible) call for us to come. Take somebody. Don't never go alone." (Unintelligible).
Who gave you the whistle?
Caretaker.
Caretaker. That's when you were making the records in New York?
Uh-huh.
